title: CycleMin imposes a joint restriction on the first-collision pair (c, t) beyond Pred cells and the cyclic-parent type
statement:
Let x be the first meeting of an initial trajectory with a hypothetical CycleMin cycle, J(c)=J(t)=x, c on the cycle, t the transient parent, c
eq t. Classifying (c,t) in E/O x E/O, CycleMin imposes a restriction on the pair (c,t) — a forbidden type both cells allow, or an order/gap/residue of (c,t) or (c,t^3) in [x^2,(x+1)^2) — that is not odd_preimage_unique / oddLanding_preimage_unique / cycleMin_not_end_odd / even_preimage_iff / odd_preimage_iff / Collision Factorization (first iff t is off-cycle; CycleMin constrains only which parent can be cyclic).
counterexamples: Collision Factorization: a cycle is forward-invariant, so first meeting at x iff t is not on the cycle; the pair is the unique cyclic parent plus any other parent
valley (O,*) empty by cycleMin_not_end_odd; odd_return_ge_n is None at n=10^6+1, 13, 125
valley (E,O) occupancy is odd-cell Type 2: empty at n=10^6+1 (Type 0); occupied at x=125 with t=25<125
mixed offset t^3-x^2 equals the archived cube-gap on all 994 Type-2 images of odd starts in [13,2001); nearest-even gap is 1 by parity
(E,E) gaps are the even widths 2,4,...,2(|Pred_E|-1); at x=10 the eleven evens 100..120 have max gap 20
named forks 100->10<-102 and 365/501 at 763 via 582276 and 582916 are (E,E); 763 has empty odd cell
notes: Phase 0 only. Not a halt theorem and not a leftover-killer. Not a reopen of the first-intersection taxonomy, the general first-collision / ancestry branch, the entry corridor, the cyclic seam, seam sliding, or twin-flight. Collision Factorization is a REPARAMETERIZATION of forward invariance plus the unique cyclic in-edge. Mixed placement is the cube-gap. No finance, no K=11, no L=55293, no floor raise. No Paper A edit, no ledger row, no new Lean.
tested_range: lemma table; valley occupancy at n=10^6+1; odd starts in [13,2001); Type-2 witness 25->125; (E,E) gaps at x=10 and by formula at the floor; named forks 100->10<-102 and 365/501 at 763
